sourceOccurrences.label: Interior normalization and positive clock
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:math/0505368v3, Theorem 3 and Remark 4; NYJM 11 (2005), pp.661–664
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Written chordal-to-radial proof and stopped inverse; arbitrary weights made explicit
sourceOccurrences.note: The explicitly normalized map gives the radial Loewner equation and the strictly positive capacity clock by differentiation and a rational vector-field identity.

sourceOccurrences.label: Mixed forces and the old target
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:math/0505368v3, Theorem 3 and Remark 4; NYJM 11 (2005), pp.661–664
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Written chordal-to-radial proof and stopped inverse; arbitrary weights made explicit
sourceOccurrences.note: Reflection pairs transport arbitrary interior and boundary forces. The residual weight kappa-6 minus the original weight sum is exactly the force at the image of the old chordal target.

sourceOccurrences.label: The inverse radial-to-chordal law
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:math/0505368v3, Theorem 3 and Remark 4; NYJM 11 (2005), pp.661–664
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Written chordal-to-radial proof and stopped inverse; arbitrary weights made explicit
sourceOccurrences.note: Local uniqueness and uniqueness of normalized maps identify the inverse law, including the compensating interior force. The stop at the new boundary target is retained.

sourceOccurrences.label: Direct disk normalization
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:math/0505368v3, Theorem 3, disk-to-disk case; NYJM 11 (2005), Theorem 3, pp.662–664
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Direct disk proof of the target-change law and its stated stopping scope
sourceOccurrences.note: Differentiating the disk normalization gives its positive capacity clock and the radial vector-field identity, with no auxiliary boundary target.

sourceOccurrences.label: Radial target changes
sourceOccurrences.locator: arXiv:math/0505368v3, Theorem 3, disk-to-disk case; NYJM 11 (2005), Theorem 3, pp.662–664
sourceOccurrences.relationship: Direct disk proof of the target-change law and its stated stopping scope
sourceOccurrences.note: The angular generator and reflected force identities give the transformed radial law with residual weight at the old target. Direct normalization retains precisely the source collision and new-interior-target stops.
